To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

clearance of Aβ from the brain is a dynamic, complex process that is mediated by several clearance systems, including transport across the blood-brain barrier and the glymphatic and lymphatic systems.
the glymphatic pathway is an important route for clearance of amyloid beta and tau, and that the glymphatics are altered in Alzheimer disease.
Aβ clearance from the brain is mediated by multiple clearance systems that act together to drive Aβ from the brain and that any alteration to these clearance systems could contribute to AD.

the question of how Aβ is removed from the brain and what happens if clearance systems are impaired.

understanding the role of the brain clearance systems in normal brain physiology and how these systems are compromised in the early stages of Alzheimer disease.

there are many clearance mechanisms in the brain and the relative contribution of each is unclear, but that astroglial clearance and the glymphatic clearance system seem to be the most important.

the glymphatic clearance is a major contributor to Aβ clearance in the brain, and that the meningeal lymphatics may play an important role in the drainage of interstitial fluid and proteins from the brain.

Aβ accumulation in the brain is the result of a failure of the clearance mechanisms.
the brain is equipped with a robust and efficient clearance system that is able to remove eAβ and other proteins from the brain.

the clearance systems of AD brains are impaired, which might contribute to AD pathogenesis.
the clearance of Aβ is not a single process but a complex interplay of different clearance mechanisms that work together in the brain.
